title: Bidayat al-Mujtahid wa Nihayat al-Muqtasid
author: ibn-rushd
attributionNote: The attribution is the one the manuscript tradition and the scholarship give.
description: Ibn Rushd's comparative account of the law, setting out each question with the positions of the Maliki, Hanafi, Shafi'i and Hanbali schools and the reasons they differ. He states the points of agreement first, then the disagreements and the evidence behind each, making the book a guide to the substance of fiqh rather than to one school's manual.
historicalContext: Written in al-Andalus and the Maghrib by a philosopher and jurist who served as a Maliki judge in Cordoba and Seville. Its comparative method reflects the plural legal world of the medieval Islamic west and made it a standard text for later comparative study.
availabilityNote: Arabic text only, streamed from OpenITI at read time. No English translation is included because no public-domain English translation was verified. Only the catalogue record, chapter outline and passage index are held here.
